pointers.sentence: Since 6.0 it builds an `email.message.EmailMessage` under a policy, `email.policy.default` unless its new policy argument names another, and the policy does the checking (`django/core/mail/message.py:EmailMessage.message`).
The value has the old classes' API but is no instance of them; the modern API is "a cleaner and Unicode-friendly interface", the release notes say (`docs/releases/6.0.txt`).

`SafeMIMEText` and `SafeMIMEMultipart` are still handed out by the package's `__getattr__`, with a warning (`django/core/mail/__init__.py:__getattr__`); `forbid_multi_line_headers` and `sanitize_address` warn when called; and `EmailMessage.attach` warns when given a legacy `email.mime.base.MIMEBase`, and since 6.0 takes an `email.message.MIMEPart`.
`BadHeaderError`, deprecated too, is now `ValueError` itself, so that code catching it catches what the policy raises (`django/core/mail/message.py:BadHeaderError`).

Alternatives are read by field name as the message is built, so one appended as a plain tuple fails then, with `AttributeError`; the release notes support adding one only by `EmailMultiAlternatives.attach_alternative` (`django/core/mail/message.py:EmailMultiAlternatives._add_bodies`).
Since 6.1 a `"Bcc"` among the extra headers raises `ValueError` when the message is built: blind copies go in the bcc argument (`django/core/mail/message.py:EmailMessage.message`).
A positional use still works and warns (`django/utils/deprecation.py:deprecate_posargs`).

As `mail_admins` or `mail_managers` sends, a list of (name, address) pairs warns and is reduced to its addresses, and a value that is not a list or tuple of strings is `ImproperlyConfigured` (`django/core/mail/__init__.py:_send_server_message`).
Since 6.1 `MAILERS` names backends by alias, as `CACHES`, `DATABASES`, `STORAGES` and `TASKS` do, for "configuring multiple email backends with different options" (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`).

Its handler, `django.core.mail.mailers`, makes at each lookup a new instance of the class an entry's `"BACKEND"` names, the SMTP backend when it names none, with the entry's `"OPTIONS"` as keyword arguments and the alias beside them (`django/core/mail/handler.py:MailersHandler.create_connection`).

In a project that does not define it, `mailers` answers `"default"` with `get_connection`, which makes the backend `EMAIL_BACKEND` names, with no alias, so that the SMTP backend reads the old settings; any other alias is `MailerDoesNotExist` (`django/core/mail/handler.py:MailersHandler`).
Unless an old email setting is defined, which warned as the settings loaded, the lookup warns that a mailer will be required (`django/core/mail/deprecation.py:warn_about_default_mailers_if_needed`):

Where `MAILERS` is defined it returns a new instance of the default mailer, its keyword arguments added to the entry's options, and refuses a backend's path with `RuntimeError` (`django/core/mail/__init__.py:get_connection`).

Some old combinations now raise (6.1). fail_silently=True, auth_user= or auth_password= beside connection= is a `TypeError`, where older versions ignored them, the documentation says (`docs/topics/email.txt`); so is any of them, or connection=, beside `using=` (`django/core/mail/deprecation.py:report_using_incompatibility`).

Some old combinations now raise (6.1). fail_silently=True, auth_user= or auth_password= beside connection= is a `TypeError`, where older versions ignored them, the documentation says (`docs/topics/email.txt`); so is any of them, or connection=, beside `using=` (`django/core/mail/deprecation.py:report_using_incompatibility`).

`EmailMessage.send` no longer stores on the message the backend it used, though it uses one set there, and raises `AttributeError` for a subclass that defines a method get_connection, which it used to call (`django/core/mail/message.py:EmailMessage.send`).

The base's support for fail_silently is deprecated: a backend that offers it keeps its own attribute, as the SMTP, console and file backends do (`django/core/mail/backends/base.py:BaseEmailBackend.__init__`).

Making the SMTP backend directly is deprecated too; such an instance reads the old settings for what it is not given, and where `MAILERS` is defined, one made in a run with only a host raised `AttributeError` as it read EMAIL_PORT (`django/core/mail/backends/smtp.py:EmailBackend.__init__`).

Two checks came with it (6.1): `"mail.W001"` warns when `MAILERS` lacks a `"default"` entry, and the deployment check `"mail.E001"` is an error when that entry names the console, file, local-memory or dummy backend (`django/core/checks/mail.py`).

Its email_backend argument is deprecated, and refused with `ImproperlyConfigured` beside `using=` or where `MAILERS` is defined; its undocumented connection method is gone, and a subclass that defines one raises `AttributeError` as it is made (`django/utils/log.py:AdminEmailHandler.__init__`).
`BrokenLinkEmailsMiddleware` takes its alias from its class attribute `BrokenLinkEmailsMiddleware.using` (`django/middleware/common.py:BrokenLinkEmailsMiddleware.send_mail`).

Without `MAILERS`, both send with fail_silently=True, as before, and leave the alias aside; with it, they send to the alias, pass no fail_silently and catch only `MailerDoesNotExist`, so an error in sending is not swallowed: in a run whose default mailer's SMTP host could not be reached, `AdminEmailHandler.emit` raised `TimeoutError` (`django/utils/log.py:AdminEmailHandler.send_mail`).

The `task` decorator turns a module-level function into a `Task`, checked against its backend as it is made; `Task.enqueue` hands it and its arguments to the task's backend of `TASKS`, which returns a `TaskResult`, the record of what became of it (`django/tasks/base.py:Task.enqueue`).
`TASKS` defaults to `ImmediateBackend`, which runs the task inside `enqueue` (`django/conf/global_settings.py`); `DummyBackend` keeps results and runs nothing.
Both are "primarily intended for development and testing", and Django "does not provide a worker mechanism to run tasks", the release notes say (`docs/releases/6.0.txt`).

Since 6.1 the decorator passes a keyword argument it does not take, all but run_after, which it refuses, to the backend's `BaseTaskBackend.task_class`: a task class that declares such a field takes it, and the built-in `Task` refuses it with a `TypeError` (`django/tasks/base.py:task`).

And since 6.1 a `Task` and a `TaskResult` can be pickled: a task pickles as its fields, its function replaced by the function's dotted path, and is made again with those fields and the function of the task the decorator bound at that path (`django/tasks/base.py:Task.__reduce__`).
